_what_this_is: the Option-2 engineering round's measurements: what the transport actually does, what the storage model was getting wrong, and what the authorized Hugging Face cleanup recovered. Measured, not argued.

measured_throughput._how: 8 MB and 32 MB POSTed to a discarding endpoint (speed.cloudflare.com/__up) from the dev box, $0, nothing stored. Consistent with the project's recorded 0.72 MB/s and far above the 0.23 MB/s bound the restore model uses.
measured_throughput._how_down: attempt5's own launcher log: probe confirmation.B.s1916380711 announced 23:26:59 and fetched and verified by 23:31:15 -- 2.22 GiB in 3.8 min. The link is ASYMMETRIC by ~15x, which is why fetching ten probes was routine and restoring them is the problem.
measured_throughput._the_direction_that_matters: only dev-box -> replacement pod. Everything else in this campaign's transport is already fast enough.

quota_endpoint_after_cleanup._how: the LFS batch endpoint answers 'would N bytes be accepted' without sending or storing anything. One probe is 2.22 GiB.

storage_model_defects_repaired.defect: `storage_requirement` charged a trained probe at `total_probes * leaf_gib` -- the size of the bf16 INITIALIZATION LEAF -- while the recipe every probe derives from declares `dtype: "float32"`. The model contradicted the config it ran under, by exactly the two dtypes' ratio.
storage_model_defects_repaired.fix: derived through `aadistill.runtime.cost.CheckpointFootprint` from the SAVE dtype read out of the frozen recipe. Nothing about this model family, parameter count or experiment is in the generic arithmetic -- every dtype is an argument, and an unknown dtype raises rather than defaulting.

storage_model_defects_repaired.defect: the training working set assumed bf16 weights; autocast changes the COMPUTE dtype, not the parameters.
storage_model_defects_repaired.fix: weights, gradient and moment count all read from the recipe.

storage_model_defects_repaired.defect: container storage and durable capacity were one number. The bytes that must merely survive teardown were charged to the pod's own disk, and the destination gate checked the dev-box store while NOTHING checked the pod's.
storage_model_defects_repaired.fix: `container_residency` and `durable_backend` are derived separately; `destination_gate` charges the derived durable requirement and a new `container_gate` charges peak local residency against the provisioned disk.

storage_model_defects_repaired.defect: nothing released a probe's local workdir. `announce_durable` runs BEFORE the transfer, so it cannot authorize a release, and there was no later point that could.
storage_model_defects_repaired.fix: a real acknowledgement boundary: the launcher writes a release ack only after the bytes arrived off-pod AND re-identified there; the driver releases acked probes before training the next one and RAISES if a release fails.

storage_model_defects_repaired.defect: every bound was a derivation, and a derivation can be wrong in the one direction that costs a session.
storage_model_defects_repaired.fix: `require_probe_headroom` measures the filesystem before each probe and refuses if it cannot hold the next one. A modelling error now costs a clean stop with every finished probe durable.

r2_identity_validated_on_a_real_probe.what_ran: the production `verify_transferred_leaf` against the bytes at a NEW local path, with the identity the durable ack announced.

r2_identity_validated_on_a_real_probe._what_this_does_NOT_cover: the network leg. A local copytree faithfully tests re-identification from ARRIVED bytes, which is R2's substance, and tests nothing about a remote backend's throughput or semantics. That is the piece still owed once a backend is chosen.

It preserves R2 for all ten probes, leaves $5.33 of margin against the campaign ceiling, and fixes the architecture rather than the arithmetic. A RunPod network volume is the obvious candidate at roughly $0.07/GB/month; it is a paid storage change and therefore a maintainer decision.

network_volume_investigation.authorized_by: maintainer, 2026-09-22: one 50 GB RunPod Standard Network Volume, cumulative storage spend capped at $1.00
network_volume_investigation._cost_basis: the volume existed about 15 minutes. At RunPod's $0.07/GB/month for volumes under 1 TB, 50 GB is $0.00486/hour, so the incurred charge is ~$0.001 and is reported as <=$0.01. Well inside the $1.00 authorization.
network_volume_investigation._why_deleted: as placed it had no working fill path, so it could not serve the purpose it was approved for, and an idle volume burns the storage authorization while the conflict below is decided. Recreating it is one API call in whichever datacenter the decision picks.

the_measured_conflict._what: the maintainer's three conditions cannot all be met today. Condition 1 wants Network Volume / S3 access; condition 2 wants L40S availability compatible with the formal continuation. Measured across all 16 storage-capable, listed datacenters, NO datacenter has both.
the_measured_conflict._l40s_is_scarce_everywhere: EU-NL-1 is the only datacenter reporting L40S at all right now, storage-capable or not, and its stock status is Low. Six non-storage datacenters were probed as a control and returned no L40S either, so a null is 'no GPU there' rather than a malformed query.
the_measured_conflict.s3_service_is_real: https://s3api-eur-is-1.runpod.io/<volume-id>/ answers HTTP 401 AccessDenied 'missing Authorization header' -- a live S3 service. s3api-eu-nl-1.runpod.io does not resolve at all, so the S3 rollout is partial and EU-NL-1 is not in it.
the_measured_conflict.s3_needs_a_key_i_cannot_mint: RunPod's S3 API uses a separate S3 API key created in the console. The GraphQL key this repository holds is not one, and no mutation in the schema creates one. Even in an S3 datacenter the transfer could not be authenticated from here.
the_measured_conflict.why_eu_nl_1_alone_does_not_solve_it: without S3, the only way bytes reach a volume is through a pod, and the dev box is the only source. EU-NL-1 offers exactly two GPU types -- L40S at $1.09/h and B300 at $7.89/h -- so the cheapest machine that can fill the volume IS the L40S. 22.2 GiB at the measured 0.68 MB/s is 584.6 minutes = $10.62 of billed L40S time, which is precisely the cost the backend was approved to eliminate.
the_measured_conflict._not_resolved_autonomously: the maintainer's instruction is explicit: do not change the approved GPU/provider class merely to accommodate the volume without returning for review. Every remaining option changes something that is the maintainer's to change.
